title: ‘Ma, they punched me’: Student’s last call to family; how horror unfolded at homestay
content: Nimisha Thakuria, a 22-year-old Gauhati University student, made a frantic phone call stating she could not breathe. After her family lost contact, she was found critically injured at a homestay on the outskirts of Guwahati. Her alleged companion, Ashiq Ali, has been detained, stating that she hanged herself. Local residents have protested for a thorough investigation, linking the incident to broader societal issues.

title: 17 killed, 15 wounded in South Africa mass shooting
content: Seventeen people were killed and fifteen injured following a shooting at a tavern in Wedela township. The shooting occurred late on Saturday night in Gauteng province, resulting in chaos among the patrons. Eight suspects reportedly armed with rifles and pistols opened fire on people inside and outside the tavern. Police have launched a manhunt and are seeking information regarding the suspects involved.

title: Slained Hamas chief's ex-bodyguard stayed as 'Mr. X' in UK, planned attacks on Jews
content: A former bodyguard linked to Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh has been apprehended in London due to his alleged involvement in planning attacks. Despite having British citizenship, his connections to Hamas's military faction raise questions about how he gained entry. This arrest, a result of a multinational operation involving Israeli intelligence, has led to extradition efforts aimed at moving him to Germany for further investigation of the accused attack scheme.

title: Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath backs PM Narendra Modi’s call for better water data
content: Nithin Kamath highlights the critical necessity for improved data on India's water resources to tackle ongoing issues. He stresses that understanding water-related challenges is essential for developing effective solutions in the future. Kamath refers to the significant dependence on groundwater for agriculture and notes the over-extraction of this resource. Additionally, he supports Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for systematic water data governance and the use of AI.

title: Vijay Kumar Sharma becomes government teacher at 59 after clearing TGT, PGT
content: At 59, Uttar Pradesh resident Vijay Kumar Sharma has achieved his long-held dream of becoming a government teacher after 27 years of attempts. Sharma, who cleared TGT written examinations six times and PGT exams four times but missed final selection, has been appointed as a Sanskrit TGT at Ailum Inter College in Shamli. His 28-year-old daughter Mamta also cleared the recruitment examination and is currently on the waiting list. Sharma is expected to serve until retirement at 62.

title: Asian Games: Sindhu, Hooda exits cap India's disappointing badminton campaign
content: At the Asian Games 2026, India's badminton team concluded with just one medal. Both PV Sindhu and Unnati Hooda exited in the women's singles quarterfinals after fierce competition. The women’s doubles team fell to a strong Malaysian pair, and mixed doubles suffered a narrow defeat. A demanding tournament schedule took its toll on performance, highlighting a stark decline from their previous edition's achievements.

title: Missouri house transformed into ‘African Queen’ listed for $1.2 million
content: A 1962 house in Springfield, Missouri, known as the African Queen, is on the market for $1.2 million. Bought by Michael and Lisa Willhoit in 2013, the 3,176-square-foot home features a 15-foot Zulu warrior sculpture, a 20,000-piece crocodile mosaic, reclaimed teak, unusual light fixtures and a glass floor overlooking spring-fed water. It is currently used as a short-term rental.

title: Long Island entrepreneur grows garage startup into award-winning security firm
content: Founded in 2020 by Jawad Khalfan, SecureTech Systems has successfully executed over 1,500 installations. The company has shifted its focus from residential services to larger commercial security projects, earning accolades including the 2026 Next-Gen Entrepreneur of the Year award. This remarkable growth is driven by impactful projects in sectors such as education, healthcare, and commerce. SecureTech's expansion as a key technology partner in New York continues to thrive.

title: Florida used robot rabbits to hunt Burmese pythons threatening the Everglades
content: Florida is testing solar-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades. Developed by the South Florida Water Management District and University of Florida, the robotic decoys mimic prey using heat and scent while AI cameras detect approaching snakes. Officials can then alert trained removal agents, adding technology to Florida’s wider python control efforts.

title: Psychiatrist explains why parents should rethink sending kids away to college
content: Parents are key players in their children's transition to college, providing essential support through discussions about substances prior to departure. Evidence suggests that effective parental communication can significantly lower the likelihood of risky behaviors involving alcohol and drugs. By fostering an open relationship, parents empower their children to seek assistance when necessary, ensuring they step into college life ready to make informed decisions and navigate challenges with confidence.

title: California buried 662,700 tires under I-880 ramp, saved $477K, 22 years
content: Engineers faced challenges while upgrading a highway interchange in Milpitas due to unstable bay mud. They opted to use shredded waste tires as lightweight fill to prevent ground settlement. This choice reduced weight on the soft soil by 40 percent and saved significant project costs. Over two decades, the infrastructure has shown no maintenance issues or structural damage.

title: ‘Old footage’: Delhi Police fact-checks viral Jantar Mantar protest video amid SIR row
content: Delhi Police has clarified that a video being shared regarding a recent protest is actually outdated material from a previous event. They have cautioned that those spreading false information could face legal consequences. Meanwhile, opposition parties are actively protesting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar due to ongoing disputes about the electoral roll revision.

title: One point short in 2018, Ahvar Rizvi gets his Asian Games chance eight years later
content: One point short of India’s 2018 Asian Games selection, Trap shooter Ahvar Rizvi spent the next seven years rebuilding his career after Double Trap was removed from the international programme. The 2018 junior world champion struggled with the transition, briefly quit shooting and later competed with teammate Lakshya Sheoran’s gun. Now, Rizvi has made his first Asian Games team and is preparing to represent India in Trap at Nagoya.

title: Former Keralam chief secretary Jiji Thomson alleges Gyanesh Kumar suggested BJP ticket
content: Jiji Thomson, a former chief secretary, revealed that Gyanesh Kumar suggested he join the BJP. The proposal occurred during a flight to New Delhi in 2016. Kumar mentioned that Thomson could become a Union minister if elected. Thomson, however, declined the suggestion, expressing disinterest in politics. He has been approached by various political leaders in the past regarding electoral positions.

title: Mohanlal's organic garden at his Elamakkara home: Actor grows bitter gourd, tomatoes, okra and more - VIDEO
content: Mohanlal, the renowned actor, has nurturing an organic vegetable garden at his Elamakkara home in Kochi for years. During the 2021 lockdown, he engaged fans by sharing videos of his gardening endeavors, showcasing that even small spaces can yield fresh produce with methods like grow bags. This variety includes vegetables used in everyday cooking, all while he juggles his thriving acting career with his passion for sustainable farming.

title: OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs summoned by Australia Senate over AI agent breach
content: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have received written requests to appear at a public hearing in Canberra on Thursday, according to a spokesperson for Senator Sarah Hanson-Young, the Australian Greens lawmaker chairing the inquiry. Neither company immediately responded to requests for comment outside business hours. Earlier, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the breach as “unacceptable”.

title: Taiwan says US understands defence needs as $14 billion arms package remains on hold
content: Taiwan's Deputy Foreign Minister, Chen Ming-chi, emphasized that the United States is well aware of Taiwan's defense needs. Currently, Taiwan is waiting for a decision on a $14 billion arms deal, which the US has temporarily stalled. President Trump referred to this deal as a significant bargaining tool after his talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Meanwhile, China is continually strengthening its military prowess, creating ongoing challenges for Taiwan.

title: AI mural inspired by Banksy sparks backlash in Bristol
content: A newly unveiled AI-generated mural at the Jolly Colliers pub in Bristol has ignited backlash from local artists. They criticized inaccuracies in the depiction of renowned landmarks and raised concerns over the mention of Banksy. While the pub owner stated that the mural is a temporary fixture due to wall conditions, the episode has underscored deeper worries about technology's influence on artistic integrity and fair compensation for creativity.

title: Rumours of ghost & ‘missing girls’ spark night-long protest at university in Punjab
content: Students at a private university in Rajpura protested due to false rumours about missing female students. The unrest began after a prank led to ghost stories linked to a supposed suicide. Police confirmed that no students were missing and that the reports were unfounded. The crowd clashed with police and vandalized vehicles during the protest. Authorities are investigating the source of the rumours while assuring that academic activities remain unaffected.

title: How 1,500 Christmas trees transformed a lake in 3 years
content: In an innovative study in southeastern Finland, researchers submerged 1,500 spruce trees in Lake Saimaa to analyze their influence on aquatic biodiversity. After a three-year period, the findings revealed a marked increase in benthic organisms. This experiment showcases how discarded Christmas trees could be creatively repurposed to foster healthier underwater ecosystems, shedding light on sustainable waste management strategies.

title: Why kids behave differently with each parent, according to psychology
content: Children often exhibit different behaviors with each parent, reflecting the unique bonds formed through daily encounters. Such variations do not signify favoritism but instead showcase patterns of emotional safety and attachment. Factors like daily routines or emotional necessities shape their interactions. These behaviors reveal the child's comfort level with each caregiver. By grasping these dynamics, parents can support their child's emotional growth without fostering rivalry.

title: Mark Feehily sues surgeon over weight-loss op that caused stomach removal
content: Westlife star Mark Feehily is suing bariatric surgeon Nick Carter in a £200,000 claim over complications following weight-loss surgery. Feehily alleges the procedure led to recurring sepsis and eventually required his entire stomach to be removed. Carter denies negligence and argues that the leak was a recognised complication of the procedure.

title: Boeing finds software glitch that may disable landing guidance on 737 MAX jets
content: Boeing also faced renewed scrutiny in January 2024 after a door plug blew out of an almost-new 737 MAX 9 operated by Alaska Airlines during a flight. The latest software issue does not mean that the aircraft is unsafe to fly. Regulators and the company are still examining the problem and determining whether any further action is required.

title: ‘Army of Robots’: Ukraine turns to machines for its most dangerous missions
content: In a bold move to boost military efficiency, Ukraine is unveiling the 'Army of Robots' initiative, focusing on automation for the battlefield. This program is set to enhance the use of robotic systems in various military operations. Particularly, unmanned ground vehicles are being adopted for logistics, evacuation, and combat support. The initiative aims to minimize human casualties while maximizing operational effectiveness, marking a pivotal shift in Ukraine's defense strategy.

title: Chess Olympiad 2026: Can India retain their gold medals on final day?
content: India face a tense final day at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, with both defending champions still in gold-medal contention. The open team needs a win over Hungary and an Uzbekistan slip-up, while the women's team face a steeper route against Georgia. Gukesh and Savitha Shri remain in individual medal contention.

title: Russia backs India's claim to UNSC seat, firmly shuts door on Germany & Japan
content: At the recent General Assembly, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov reaffirmed Russia's support for India and Brazil to secure permanent membership on the UN Security Council. He criticized the prospect of additional seats for Western countries like Germany and Japan, linking it to the West's military actions in Ukraine, which he argues undermine core principles of the UN.

title: Chadwick Boseman's widow calls brothers' $3.4M estate lawsuit a PR stunt

Her legal response says she distributed the required assets and paid $150,000 to Derrick and Kevin from SAG-AFTRA residuals. Ledward’s attorney called the brothers’ case a “public-relations stunt” and denied claims of estate mismanagement.

title: Harassed, complained, forced to quit: Employee's viral post

Despite reporting the incidents to HR, her cries for help were dismissed, leading to even more obstacles, including pressure toward her coworkers to file complaints against her. Ultimately, she felt compelled to leave, convinced that the situation would remain unchanged.

title: ‘No jealousy’: Jurel reveals what Sooryavanshi does others ‘can’t even dream of’

With exceptional skills and standout performances, he has captured the interest of cricket enthusiasts on a global scale. Dhruv Jurel, who competes alongside him, acknowledges the singular nature of Sooryavanshi's abilities. Although Jurel has found success in recent games, he believes comparisons to Sooryavanshi are unwarranted, as the young talent's impact resonates profoundly in the sport.

title: Winds, floods, 20-foot waves: What’s behind the nor’easter battering US East Coast
content: A powerful nor’easter is currently disrupting life on the US East Coast, delivering heavy rainfall and fierce winds. More than 100,000 households are without power due to downed trees and lines. Air travel has come to a standstill with numerous cancellations and delays across airports. Coastal regions are on alert for possible flooding from exceptionally high tides, while emergency teams remain on standby for further challenges as the storm unfolds.

Anushka Sharma's order of chole bhature for Virat Kohli further enhanced demand, leading to the expansion of the restaurant from one to four outlets. Monthly revenue skyrocketed from ₹1-1.5 lakh to nearly ₹2 crore.

The sisters received recognition for their volunteer efforts as they also contributed to local families in need. Their fundraising initiative concluded in 2026, marking its final season.

content: the project represents a dramatic departure from the property James purchased in 2020 . the los Angeles lakers star paid $36.75 million for the 2.72-acre property in 2020, acquiring a historic estate that dated to the 1930s . three years later the original house was demolished .

title: Avalanche strikes Nepal's Himlung Himal base camp, 10 missing
content: the avalanche hit the base camp of Himlung Himal in western Nepal . two members of his kitchen staff were among those missing . climbers evacuated after a weather warning was issued last week . the region had received heavy snowfall for several days .

title: ‘Congress part of every conspiracy’: CM Yogi amid 'dissent within EC' row
content: chief minister defended the election commission amid "dissent within the poll body" row . he slammed the Congress party for "creating confusion and targeting constitutional institutions" despite this history, the uproar raised by the Congress, Samajwadi Party, RJD .

title: $50 Hamptons barn find turns into C$290k: Lost 1912 Emily Carr sells big
content: a barn sale in the Hamptons is not where most people expect to encounter a significant work of Canadian art . the canvas was authenticated as a 1912 work by Emily Carr, one of Canada's most celebrated artists . an unexpected find turned an overlooked painting into one of the more remarkable bargain finds to reach the auction market in 2024 .

title: Lake 227 algae blooms continued decades after nitrogen was removed
content: lake 227, part of the Experimental Lakes Area, began receiving carefully measured additions of nitrogen and phosphorus in 1969 . researchers reduced nitrogen inputs during the 1970s and stopped adding nitrogen entirely in 1990 . but the lake remained highly eutrophic, with algal blooms continuing year after year .

title: SIR row: Congress' Khera questions EC over Form 6, says Bengal & Bihar polls ‘illegal’
content: Congress leader questioned the Election Commission's response to concerns over Form 6 . Khera alleged that the SIR exercise was based on an "illegally changed" form . he questioned whether the election Commission had addressed objections raised by Election Commissioners .

title: EC to audit ECINET independently after allegations of access issues
content: a full meeting of the Election Commission of India on saturday decided to exempt electors who have got notices for being unmapped to the last SIR or over logical discrepancies . the EC also agreed to an independent audit of ECINET software though it rejected allegations that EROs were being locked out .
